group.passage: Every Saturday and Sunday in October, a nature club led walks along the wooden path beside the mangrove forest near MRT Hongshulin Station in Tamsui. Eight people who joined these walks on different days later left comments on the club’s web page.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Amy
passage_parts.text: I loved the “water pens”! Our guide showed us long green seedlings that hang from the branches like pens. They begin to grow while they are still on the tree. When they are ready, they drop into the mud below.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Ben
passage_parts.text: I joined a Sunday morning walk, but it was high tide. The mud was under water, and only the tops of the trees stood above it. I didn’t see a single crab. Next time, I’ll choose a walk at low tide.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Cindy
passage_parts.text: We went on a Saturday afternoon, when the tide was low. My son watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes. He had never seen so many of them in one place. Now he wants to come back with his camera.

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: David
passage_parts.text: My favorite part was the mudskippers. They are fish, but they hop around on the mud like little frogs. I didn’t know that a fish could spend so much time out of the water!

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Emma
passage_parts.text: Honestly, I was a little bored. It was hot, the path was crowded, and the mud did not smell good. Next time, I think I’d rather spend the day at the beach.

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Frank
passage_parts.text: I didn’t know that this area has been a nature reserve since 1986. Visitors are not allowed to walk into the forest itself, so we stayed on the wooden path the whole time.

passage_parts.label: G
passage_parts.title: Grace
passage_parts.text: Bring something to help you see birds far away! I saw white egrets walking slowly through the mud, looking for food. Our guide said that many other birds come here every winter.

passage_parts.label: H
passage_parts.title: Henry
passage_parts.text: The guide explained that these trees can live in salty water, which most plants can’t do. Their roots spread wide in the soft mud and help hold the trees in place.

questions.stem: In Emma’s comment, which adjective means “full of too many people, so that it is hard to move around”?（簡答題，2分）

1.explanation_zh: Cindy 說 My son watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes（兒子在泥灘上看招潮蟹看了二十分鐘）。spend＋時間＋V-ing＝花時間做某事，所以 watched 要改成 watching。
evidence: My son watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes.
1.strategy_zh: 用 boy、crabs on the mud 回到 Cindy 的留言；spend a long time 後面的動詞改成 V-ing。
hints: 回到 Cindy 的留言：她兒子在泥灘上花了二十分鐘做什麼？
原文 My son ___ the fiddler crabs on the mud；把這個動詞改成 V-ing。

2.explanation_zh: Amy 說導覽員給大家看長長的綠色小苗 that hang from the branches like pens（像筆一樣掛在樹枝上），這也是這種樹叫「水筆仔」（water pens）的原因。look like 後面接複數名詞 pens，照抄即可。
evidence: Our guide showed us long green seedlings that hang from the branches like pens.
2.strategy_zh: 用 young plants、hang from 回到 Amy 的留言；看小苗像什麼東西，照抄複數名詞。
hints: look like 後面要接名詞；小苗不只一根，用複數。
回到 Amy 的留言：掛在樹枝上的綠色小苗看起來像什麼？
原文 hang from the branches like ___；照抄這個名詞。

3.explanation_zh: 正確的是 B、D、F。B：Amy 說小苗還在樹上時就開始生長（They begin to grow while they are still on the tree）。D：Frank 說遊客不准走進樹林，所以全程都待在木棧道上。F：Henry 說導覽員解釋這些樹能活在鹹水裡。C、E 都要對照 Ben 和 Cindy 兩則留言：引言說留言的人是在不同日子參加導覽，Ben 參加的那場剛好漲潮，泥灘在水下、一隻螃蟹也沒看到；Cindy 那場是退潮，泥灘露出來，她兒子看了二十分鐘的招潮蟹。所以 C（泥灘整天在水下）被 Cindy 的留言推翻，E（任何時間都看得到螃蟹）被 Ben 的留言推翻。A 八則留言都沒有提到租船。
evidence: They begin to grow while they are still on the tree.
Visitors are not allowed to walk into the forest itself, so we stayed on the wooden path the whole time.
The guide explained that these trees can live in salty water, which most plants can’t do.

option_notes_zh.A: 八則留言都沒有提到租船遊覽（NM）；Frank 只說遊客不能走進樹林，全程待在木棧道上。
option_notes_zh.C: 只看 Ben 的留言好像成立（漲潮時泥灘在水下），但他說的是 high tide 那一場；Cindy 那場退潮（the tide was low），兒子在泥灘上看招潮蟹，可見泥灘不是整天泡在水裡（CT）。
option_notes_zh.E: 只看 Cindy 的留言好像成立（退潮時看到很多招潮蟹），但 Ben 漲潮時那一場一隻螃蟹都沒看到（I didn’t see a single crab），所以不是任何時間都看得到（CT）。

3.strategy_zh: 跨留言判斷：每個選項先找出相關的留言，再看其他留言有沒有補充或推翻；注意引言說大家是在不同日子參加，Ben 和 Cindy 遇到的潮水不一樣。只看一則留言就下結論，容易選到 C、E。
hints: 每個選項都要找到明寫的留言，還要看其他留言有沒有說相反的情況。
小苗、木棧道、鹹水各出現在誰的留言？
比較 Ben（漲潮）和 Cindy（退潮）的留言：這會讓哪兩個選項不成立？

A: Visitors are not allowed to walk into the forest itself, so we stayed on the wooden path the whole time.
B: They begin to grow while they are still on the tree.
C: We went on a Saturday afternoon, when the tide was low.
My son watched the fiddler crabs on the mud for twenty minutes.
D: Visitors are not allowed to walk into the forest itself, so we stayed on the wooden path the whole time.
E: I joined a Sunday morning walk, but it was high tide.
I didn’t see a single crab.
F: The guide explained that these trees can live in salty water, which most plants can’t do.

4.explanation_zh: Emma 說她覺得有點無聊：天氣很熱、the path was crowded（步道很擁擠）、泥巴也不好聞。crowded 是形容詞，意思是「擠滿人的、擁擠的」。
evidence: It was hot, the path was crowded, and the mud did not smell good.
4.strategy_zh: 依英文定義找字：題目限定 Emma 的留言、限定形容詞；找她抱怨步道的那個字。
hints: 要找一個形容詞，意思是「擠滿太多人、難以走動的」。
看 Emma 的留言：她對步道有什麼不滿？
答案在 the path was ___；寫這個形容詞。

translation_zh.text:
【引言】十月的每個星期六、星期日，一個自然社團都會帶大家沿著淡水捷運紅樹林站附近、紅樹林旁的木棧道散步導覽。八位在不同日子參加導覽的人，事後在社團網頁上留言。
【A Amy】我好喜歡「水筆仔」！導覽員給我們看長長的綠色小苗，像一支支筆掛在樹枝上。它們還在樹上時就開始生長，等準備好了，就掉進下面的泥巴裡。
【B Ben】我參加的是星期日早上的導覽，可是剛好漲潮。泥灘都在水底下，只有樹梢露出水面。我連一隻螃蟹都沒看到。下次我要選退潮時的場次。
【C Cindy】我們是星期六下午去的，那時候退潮。我兒子在泥灘上看招潮蟹看了二十分鐘。他從來沒在同一個地方看過這麼多招潮蟹。現在他說想帶相機再來。
【D David】我最喜歡的是彈塗魚。牠們是魚，卻像小青蛙一樣在泥巴上跳來跳去。我以前都不知道魚可以離開水這麼久！
【E Emma】老實說，我覺得有點無聊。天氣很熱，步道很擁擠，泥巴的味道也不好聞。下次我寧可去海邊玩一天。
【F Frank】我之前不知道這裡從 1986 年起就是自然保留區。遊客不准走進樹林裡，所以我們全程都待在木棧道上。
【G Grace】記得帶能看遠處鳥兒的東西！我看到白色的白鷺在泥灘上慢慢走著找食物。導覽員說，每年冬天還有很多其他的鳥會來這裡。
【H Henry】導覽員解釋，這些樹能活在鹹水裡，這是大多數植物辦不到的。它們的根在柔軟的泥巴裡向四周伸展，幫忙把樹固定住。
